source_text: τὸ καθαρὸν καὶ ἀκίβδηλον ὑποσημαίνουσιν. Τουτὶ δὲ ἡμῖν ἐξησκηκόσιν, ἐφεῖται μὲν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν ἐσωτέραν σκηνὴν, προσκομίζειν δὲ τῷ Θεῷ θυσίας πνευματικὰς, καὶ ὡς ἐν τάξει θυμιαμάτων τῆς εὐαγγελικῆς πολιτείας καθιεροῦν οἱονείπως τὴν εὐοσμίαν. Παρεγγυᾷ δὲ χρησίμως ἀπονίζεσθαι δεῖν τοὺς εἰς τὰ Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων εἰσελαύνειν ἐθέλοντας, καὶ τῶν ἱερῶν ἔργων ἐπιμελητὰς, ἵνα μὴ ἀποθάνωσιν. Χρῆμα γὰρ ἐπισφαλὲς καὶ ἐπιζήμιον ἀληθῶς, τὸ ἐγγίζειν Θεῷ μὴ κεκαθαρμένους. Τοιγάρτοι καὶ σοφὸς ἡμῖν ἐπισκήπτει Παῦλος, εἰ τῆς μυστικῆς εὐλογίας μεταλαχεῖν ἐθέλοιμεν, ἑαυτοὺς δοκιμάζειν, προσιέναι τε οὕτω λοιπόν. Πρᾶγμα δὲ ὅτι καὶ κινδύνου μεστὸν τὸ ἀτημελὲς ἐν τούτοις, ἐκκαλύπτει λέγων· «Διὰ τοῦτο ἐν ὑμῖν πολλοὶ ἀσθενεῖς καὶ ἄῤῥωστοι, καὶ κοιμῶνται ἱκανοί. Εἰ γὰρ ἑαυτοὺς ἐκρίνομεν, οὐκ ἂν ἐκρινόμεθα. Κρινόμενοι δὲ ὑπὸ Κυρίου, παιδευόμεθα, ἵνα μὴ σὺν τῷ κόσμῳ κατακριθῶμεν.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἄραρεν οὖν ὅτι τὴν διὰ τοῦ ἁγίου βαπτίσματος ὁ ἱερὸς ἡμῖν λουτὴρ προκατεδείκνυε χάριν. {ΚΥΡ.} Ὧδε ἔχει· μὴ γὰρ ἐνδοιάσῃς ὅλως. Καὶ τόν γε τῆς τούτου κατασκευῆς περιαθρήσας τρόπον, κατατεθηπὼς ἂν, οἶμαι, καὶ ἔτι μειζόνως ἔσῃ. Γέγραπται γὰρ ὡδὶ περὶ τοῦ Βεσελεὴλ, τοῦ τὰ ἐν τῇ σκηνῇ τετεχνουργηκότος· «Οὗτος ἐποίησε τὸν λουτῆρα τὸν χαλκοῦν, καὶ τὴν βάσιν αὐτοῦ χαλκῆν, ἐκ τῶν κατόπτρων τῶν νηστευσασῶν, αἳ ἐνήστευσαν παρὰ τὰς θύρας τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου, ἐν ᾗ ἡμέρᾳ ἔπηξεν αὐτήν. Καὶ ἐποίησε τὸν λουτῆρα, ἵνα νίπτωνται ἐξ αὐτοῦ Μωσῆς τε καὶ Ἀαρὼν καὶ οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῶν καὶ τοὺς πόδας, εἰσπορευομένων αὐτῶν εἰς τὴν σκηνὴν τοῦ μαρτυρίου, οἳ ὅταν προσπορεύωνται εἰς τὸ θυσιαστήριον, λειτουργεῖν, ἐνίπτοντο ἐξ αὐτοῦ, καθάπερ συνέταξεν ὁ Κύριος τῷ Μωσῇ.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ τί τῶν κατόπτρων τὸ χρῆμα; τίνες δὲ ἄρα καὶ αἱ νηστεύσασαι; {ΚΥΡ.} Πολλὰ τῶν γεγενημένων σαφῆ μὲν οὐκ ἔχει παρὰ τῇ θείᾳ Γραφῇ τὴν ἀφήγησιν. Σημαίνεται δέ πως ἐκ παραδρομῆς, καθάπερ ἀμέλει καὶ τόδε τὸ ἐν χερσί. Ποῦ γὰρ, ἢ τίνες νενηστεύκασι τῆς ἁγίας ἐγηγερμένης σκηνῆς, οὐ λελάληκεν ὁ Μωσῆς. Ὅτι δὲ γέγονεν, οὐκ ἐνδοιάσαι τις ἄν· εἴρηται γὰρ, εἰ καὶ μὴ σαφῶς. Ἀλλὰ τουτὶ δὴ μεθέντες, ἐπ' ἐκεῖνο ἴωμεν, εἰ δοκεῖ. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Τὸ ποῖον; {ΚΥΡ.} Τὰ νενηστευκότα γύναια τίνος ἂν εἶεν εἰς τύπον; τί δὲ τὸ ἐκ τῶν κατόπτρων τὸν λουτῆρα πλάττεσθαι τὸν χαλκοῦν; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ μὴν, σὸν ἤδη πως καὶ τοῦτο εἰπεῖν. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἄκουε δή· Λελατρεύκασιν εἰδώλοις οἱ ἐξ Ἰσραὴλ, τὴν ὑπὸ τοῖς Αἰγυπτίοις ἀνατλάντες θητείαν, καὶ τοῖς ἐκείνων διαβιοῦντες νόμοις, μακροὺς διατετελέκασι χρόνους. Ἔθος τοίνυν Αἰγυπτίων μάλιστα γυναιξὶν, εἰσφοιτᾷν ἱεροῖς, λινῇ μὲν ἐσθῆτι κατεσταλμέναις, κατόπτρῳ δὲ τὴν ἀριστερὰν, καὶ σείστρῳ τὴν δεξιὰν ἱεροπρεπῶς κατεστεμμέναις, αἳ ὅτι
pass_a_gloss: [Completes the §21 sentence: to katharon kai akibdēlon hyposēmainousin, rendered at end of §21.] To us who have exēskēkosin (practiced/trained in) this, it is epheitai (permitted) to enter the esōtera skēnē (inner tent), to bring (proskomizein) thysias pneumatikas to God, and as en taxei thymiamatōn (in the rank/place of incenses) kathieroun (consecrate) hoioneipōs (in a way) the euosmia (good fragrance) of the euangelikē politeia (Gospel way of life). He parengya (enjoins) chrēsimōs that those wishing eiselaunein (to go in) into the Holies of holies, and epimelētai (overseers) of the sacred works, must wash, hina mē apothanōsin. For it is a chrēma episphales (perilous) and epizēmion (harmful) truly, to engizein (draw near) to God mē kekatharmenous (not cleansed). Therefore sophos Paul episkēptei (charges) us, if we wish metalachein (to partake) of the mystikē eulogia (mystical blessing), to dokimazein (test) ourselves and so then to come forward (prosienai). That atēmeles (carelessness) in these is kindynou meston (full of danger) he reveals, 1 Cor 11:30-32: therefore many among you astheneis and arrōstoi (weak and sick), and koimōntai hikanoi (a good number sleep); if we judged (ekrinomen) ourselves we would not be judged; judged by the Lord we are paideuometha (disciplined), so that we may not be katakrithōmen (condemned) with the kosmos. PALL: Araren (it is fixed) that the hieros loutēr prokatedeiknye (showed in advance) the charis through holy baptism. CYR: So it is; mē endoiasēs (do not doubt) at all. Having looked round (periathrēsas) at the tropos of its kataskeuē, you will be katatethēpōs (amazed) still more. Written about Beseleēl (Bezalel), who tetechnourgēkotos (crafted) the things in the tent, Exod 38:26-27 LXX: he made the bronze laver and its bronze base ek tōn katoptrōn tōn nēsteusasōn (from the mirrors of the women who fasted), who fasted at the doors of the tent of witness on the day he epēxen (pitched/fixed) it; he made the laver so that Moses, Aaron and his sons might wash hands and feet from it when entering the tent; when they approached the altar leitourgein they washed from it, as the Lord synetaxen (commanded) Moses. PALL: What is the chrēma (matter) of the mirrors? Who are the women who fasted? CYR: Many of the things that happened do not have clear aphēgēsis (narration) in divine Scripture; they are signified ek paradromēs (in passing), as indeed this matter en chersi (at hand). For where or who fasted when the holy tent had been raised (egēgermenēs), Moses did not say. That it happened, none could doubt; it is said, though not clearly. Leaving this (methentes), let us go to that, ei dokei. PALL: Which? CYR: Of what would the women (gynaia) who fasted be eis typon? What is it that the bronze laver is plattesthai (moulded) from the mirrors? PALL: Indeed, it is yours already to say this too. CYR: Hear then: the Israelites lelatreukasin (served) idols, having anatlantes (endured) the thēteia (servitude) under the Egyptians, and living by their nomoi, diatetelekasi (continued) makrous chronous. Custom of the Egyptians, especially for women, eisphoitan (to frequent) temples, katestalmenai (dressed) in linē esthēs (linen clothing), hieroprepōs katestemmenai (adorned in a priestly/sacred manner) with a katoptron (mirror) in the left and a seistron (sistrum) in the right, hai hoti [continues §23: malista tōn allōn exeilegmenai ...].

PALL: Ἄραρεν (it is fixed) that the ἱερὸς λουτήρ προκατεδείκνυε (showed in advance) the χάρις through holy baptism. CYR: So it is; μὴ ἐνδοιάσῃς (do not doubt) at all. pass_b_english: Cyril: Once we have trained ourselves in this, we are allowed to enter the inner tent, to bring spiritual sacrifices to God (1 Peter 2:5), and, as if in place of incense, to consecrate in a sense the sweet fragrance of the Gospel way of life. And he gives the useful instruction that those who wish to go into the Holy of Holies, and those who have charge of the sacred works, must wash, so that they may not die (Exodus 30:20–21). For it is a perilous and truly harmful thing to draw near to God without being cleansed. That is why the wise Paul charges us, if we wish to share in the mystical blessing, to examine ourselves and only then to come forward (1 Corinthians 11:28). And he reveals that carelessness in these matters is full of danger, when he says, ‘That is why many among you are weak and sick, and a good number have fallen asleep. For if we judged ourselves, we would not be judged. But when we are judged by the Lord, we are disciplined, so that we may not be condemned along with the world’ (1 Corinthians 11:30–32).
Palladius: It is settled, then, that the sacred laver pointed in advance to the grace that comes to us through holy baptism.

Cyril: So it is; do not doubt it at all. And if you look closely at how it was made, you will, I think, be still more amazed. For this is written about Bezalel, who crafted the furnishings of the tent: ‘He made the bronze laver and its bronze base from the mirrors of the women who fasted, who fasted at the doors of the tent of witness on the day he pitched it’ (Exodus 38:8). ‘And he made the laver so that Moses and Aaron and his sons might wash their hands and their feet from it when they went into the tent of witness; whenever they approached the altar to minister, they washed from it, just as the Lord had commanded Moses’ (Exodus 40:31–32).
Palladius: And what is this matter of the mirrors? And who were the women who fasted?

Cyril: Many things that took place are not clearly narrated in divine Scripture; they are indicated somehow in passing, as is indeed the case with the matter before us. For Moses did not say where the women fasted, or who they were, when the holy tent had been set up. But that it happened, no one could doubt, for it is stated, even if not clearly. But let us leave this and go on to that other point, if you agree.
Cyril: What might the women who fasted be a figure of? And what does it mean that the bronze laver was shaped from the mirrors?
Palladius: Well, it is for you to tell me this too.

Cyril: Listen, then. The Israelites served idols while they endured slavery under the Egyptians, and they spent long years living by the Egyptians’ laws. Now it was a custom among the Egyptians, especially for the women, to go regularly to the temples dressed in linen garments, solemnly adorned with a mirror in the left hand and a sistrum in the right; these were women who,

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 9 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

The Greek section opens with τὸ καθαρὸν καὶ ἀκίβδηλον ὑποσημαίνουσιν, which completes the last sentence of §21 and is rendered there. The first paragraph continues Cyril's turn; it carries the 'Cyril:' label like the other Book 9 rows. The section ends mid-sentence: the relative αἳ ὅτι ('women who, as ...') is left for §23, whose Greek continues μάλιστα τῶν ἄλλων ἐξειλεγμέναι; the relative is now rendered at the end of §22 ('these were women who,'), so the §23 English ('…chosen out above all the others ... were barely counted worthy') completes it; ὅτι μάλιστα is the idiom 'most especially'. The Bezalel quotation is LXX Exodus 38:26-27 (Rahlfs). Its first sentence matches Hebrew/English Exodus 38:8, where the women 'served' or 'ministered' at the entrance (LXX 'fasted'); Cyril's argument rests on the LXX 'fasted', so that is kept. Its second sentence has no counterpart in Hebrew chapter 38 but matches Exodus 40:31-32, so it is cited there. 'The mystical blessing' (μυστικὴ εὐλογία) is Cyril's usual name for the Eucharist; kept as written. Cyril's 1 Corinthians 11:31 reads ἐκρίνομεν where the New Testament text has διεκρίνομεν; the sense 'judged ourselves' is the same. 'Spiritual sacrifices' (θυσίας πνευματικάς) matches 1 Peter 2:5 word for word, so it is cited. 'Served idols ... in Egypt' may echo Joshua 24:14 or Ezekiel 20:7-8; left uncited as doubtful. 'Sistrum' is the Egyptian rattle used in the cult of Isis; kept as the plain English name of the instrument.
